record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two. Suppose that for every n, m ≥ 1, the algebraic curve A^{∘n}(x) − B^{∘m}(y) = 0 has a factor of genus 0 or 1. Must it follow that either both A and B are special (that is, Lattès maps or maps conjugate to z^±n or ±T_n for some n ≥ 2), or else A and B have a common iterate, meaning that A^{∘k} = B^{∘l} for some k, l ≥ 1?

evidence.quote: We will call a rational function special if it is either a Latt`es map or it is conjugate to z^±n, n ≥ 2, or ±T_n, n ≥ 2, where T_n is the nth Chebyshev polynomial.

Conjecture 4.2. Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two such that all algebraic curves (12) have a factor of genus zero or one. Then either both A and B are special or there exist k, l ≥ 1 such that A^{∘k} = B^{∘l}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^1$ denote the Riemann sphere. A rational function $R:\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^1$ is called *special* if it is either a Lattès map (i.e., a rational function arising as the quotient by a finite group action of an endomorphism of an elliptic curve) or it is conjugate (via a Möbius transformation) to $z^{\pm n}$ for some integer $n\geq 2$ or to $\pm T_n$ for some integer $n\geq 2$, where $T_n$ denotes the $n$th Chebyshev polynomial. For a rational function $R$ and an integer $k\geq 1$, let $R^{\circ k}$ denote the $k$-fold iterate $R\circ R\circ\cdots\circ R$.

Let $A$ and $B$ be rational functions of degree at least two, and assume that for every pair of integers $n,m\geq 1$ the algebraic curve in $\mathbb{C}^2$ defined by
$$A^{\circ n}(x) - B^{\circ m}(y) = 0$$
has at least one irreducible component of geometric genus $0$ or $1$.

Prove or disprove: under this hypothesis, either
(i) both $A$ and $B$ are special, or
(ii) $A$ and $B$ admit a common iterate, i.e., there exist integers $k,l\geq 1$ such that $A^{\circ k} = B^{\circ l}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears to be a stated open problem of Pakovich. Related results have been proved—e.g., Pakovich's theorem that tame rational functions whose orbits intersect infinitely often share a common iterate, and a description of pairs $(A,U)$ such that $A^{\circ d}(x)-U(y)=0$ has a genus 0 or 1 factor for all $d\geq 1$—but no source indicates that the full conjecture (allowing both $A$ and $B$ to be iterated) has been settled.

status_evidence.title: Tame rational functions: Decompositions of iterates and orbit intersections
status_evidence.snippet: If tame rational functions A and B have orbits with infinite intersection, then A and B have a common iterate.
status_evidence.claim: Special case (tame functions, orbit intersection) is solved, but the general genus-0/1 curve hypothesis remains a conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Algebraic curves A^{∘l}(x)-U(y)=0 and arithmetic of orbits of rational functions
status_evidence.snippet: Description of pairs of complex rational functions A and U of degree at least two such that for every d≥1 the algebraic curve A^◦d(x)-U(y)=0 has a factor of genus zero or one.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results are known when only A is iterated; the symmetric two-sided iteration version remains conjectural.
